model: Underlying-profit AFFO-style FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: Properties for sale, attributable realisable value
equity_bridge.note: Properties for sale HK$13,833m consolidated at 30-Jun-2026 (interim balance sheet, 0101.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:1745; FY2025 split: mainland 7,429 incl. 2,913 under development, HK 6,843 incl. 4,690 under development at Shouson Hill / Wilson Road). x0.95 attributable x0.80 realisation (selling costs, LAT/tax, cost to complete the HK sites, recent sub-cost mainland sales and the HK$124m H1-26 provision) = 10,513; discounted ~3 years at 10.5% (x0.741) = 7,790. Conservative in one respect: the debt that funds this inventory keeps its interest inside the perpetual stream, so the interest saving from repaying it with sale proceeds is NOT credited.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0%) diverges sharply from statutory EPS (-24%/yr 3yr; FY2020 loss makes the 5yr undefined) and underlying EPS (-11%/yr 3yr, FY2022 0.93 -> FY2025 0.65). EPS is distorted by revaluation deficits and by scrip dilution (4,499m -> 5,057m shares); equity is propped by RMB translation gains in OCI. None of these is a usable forward growth rate; the scenario paths are built from leasing revenue and the H1-2026 run-rate instead.
historical_growth.notes: Statutory revenue includes lumpy property sales (FY2024 1,538 vs FY2025 264), so revenue CAGRs are noisy; leasing + hotel revenue fell 10,316 -> 9,686 FY2023-25 (RMB translation and mainland office weakness) before turning up 5% in H1-2026. 'FCF' CAGRs are on Metrics.csv FCF less SBC (interest income not deducted: the company is in net debt) and are meaningless here -- FY2020-22 FCF was depressed by peak development capex (HK$12bn/yr FY2018-19) and FY2025 is flattered by the capex roll-off; they are not used. The owner-FCF series that matters is the AFFO analogue in inputs.stream_definition.

scenario_narratives.base: Mainland luxury retail continues its selective recovery (H1-26 mall revenue +6% in RMB, 96% occupancy) while mainland offices (revenue -12% in H1-26, weaker-city towers 72-78% occupied) stabilise rather than recover. Westlake 66 ramps over 2026-28 and is the main source of ~6%/yr leasing growth in FY2026-27; Hong Kong retail edges up on visitor arrivals while HK office stays competitive. Interest stops being capitalised as projects complete, holding the margin near 26.5-27% before lease-up lifts it to 30%. Development spend falls to maintenance plus modest AEI once the HK$4.8bn commitment tail is paid and the V.3 projects go asset-light, so FCFE rises from ~HK$0.8bn in FY2026 to ~HK$3.2bn by the end of the decade. The dividend keeps leaning on scrip. Inventory is sold down over ~3 years below book.
scenario_narratives.bull: A stronger mainland consumption cycle and RMB appreciation (69% of net assets are RMB) lift flagship mall rents faster; Westlake 66, Center 66 Wuxi and the Plaza 66 Pavilion lease up ahead of plan; mainland office vacancy turns; the new consumer-retail CEO (Leo Tsoi, from 1-Oct-2026) sharpens tenant mix in the weaker 'zombie-mall' cities. Rates fall, cutting the 3.8% average cost of debt on a 60%-floating book, which goes straight to the post-interest margin (32.5%). The V.3 asset-light shift keeps capex at maintenance levels.
scenario_narratives.bear: Mainland luxury spending relapses (consumer confidence still ~90, tariff/geopolitical shock from the Middle East conflict flagged in the H1-26 outlook), secondary-city malls (Forum 66 Shenyang, Heartland 66 Wuhan, Riverside 66 Tianjin) keep losing share, mainland office rents keep falling and HK office reversions stay negative; the RMB weakens against the HKD peg. Westlake 66 leases slowly while its interest is already expensed, and with HK$47bn of net debt, 60% floating and interest cover ~3x, any rise in rates or refinancing spreads compresses the post-interest margin to 24.5%. Management keeps committing capital to new mainland projects at low returns (the pattern that took underlying ROE to ~2.4%), holding capex at 6% of revenue. Inventory realises well below book.
scenario_narratives.base_weight_reason: Recurring rental franchise with 96% mainland mall occupancy, investment-grade funding access (HK$10bn syndicated loan, HK$21bn undrawn facilities at FY2025) and no balance-sheet stress -- the central outcome is slow, steady growth.
scenario_narratives.bull_weight_reason: Needs several things together: mainland luxury recovery, office stabilisation, RMB strength, lower rates and capex discipline.
scenario_narratives.bear_weight_reason: Concentrated China consumption/property exposure, falling underlying EPS since FY2022, meaningful floating-rate leverage, a CEO transition, and a controlling family with a record of reinvesting at low returns rather than returning capital.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Hang Lung Properties is valued as a landlord, not as an operating company: the recurring, post-interest, post-tax, post-minority underlying profit from leasing and hotels -- with capitalised interest treated as a real cost -- less maintenance and equity-funded development capex, is capitalised at a 10.5% HKD cost of equity with no further net-debt deduction. Revaluation gains and losses are excluded entirely. Trading inventory is valued once in the bridge at a realisation haircut. Book NAV (HK$26.6/share) is a memo only: the assets earn ~2.4% on book, which is why the market pays ~0.25x.
key_risks_to_valuation: Interest-rate and refinancing risk: HK$53.6bn borrowings, 60% floating; each 100bp on the floating book is ~HK$320m pre-tax, ~10% of the FY0 stream
Mainland luxury consumption relapse hitting flagship mall rents (Plaza 66, Grand Gateway 66)
Continued mainland office rent declines (vacancy ~25% industry-wide)
RMB/HKD translation: ~69% of net assets and most leasing revenue are RMB
Capital allocation: renewed large mainland commitments would push capex above the 5.5% steady state
Scrip dividend dilution at prices below intrinsic value transfers value from cash-electing holders
CEO transition to an external consumer-retail executive (Leo Tsoi, effective 1-Oct-2026)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 6.38-10.30
data_sources.financials: Hang Lung Properties FY2025 Annual Report (financial highlights, financial review, notes 16/24, ten-year summary) and 2026 Interim Report (results highlights, notes 12/16, balance sheet); Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis in 0101.HK.duckdb
data_sources.qualitative: 0101.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-11); parent Hang Lung Group 0010.HK DCF for method and CoE consistency

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report note (staff costs): employee share-based payments HK$54m (2024: HK$74m), 0101.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:9449; H1-2026 HK$19m (0101.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:2111). Option scheme, no net-share settlement, so no equity-award taxes. SBC is already expensed inside underlying net profit; the engine margin is grossed up by the same 0.5pp so it is charged exactly once.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:05Z regular close (Yahoo chart API; last HKEX session before valuation date)
inputs.share_count_basis: 5,203m ordinary shares issued at 30-Jun-2026 (interim note 12, 0101.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:2288, after 146m scrip shares issued 15-Jun-2026) plus ~2m dilutive options (H1-2026 diluted-EPS reconciliation) = 5,205m. Held flat. The count has risen 4,499m -> 5,203m since FY2023 entirely through the scrip dividend (genuine non-SBC issuance, at HK$8.04-9.06). It is not projected forward: scrip issuance is a choice of the electing shareholders themselves, the cash retained is already inside the FCFE stream (it funds the capex line), and projecting it would charge the same retained cash twice. The 2026 interim dividend scrip (arrangement announced 30-Jul-2026, ~Sep/Oct 2026 allotment) is not yet in the count; at HK$0.12/share it is at most ~90m shares (~1.7%).
inputs.stream_definition: Revenue base = FY2025 consolidated property-leasing + hotel revenue (9,389 + 297 = 9,686; 0101.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:11311). Property-sales revenue (264, lumpy and loss-making) is excluded from the growth base and valued once via inventory in the equity bridge. 'EBITDA margin' is NOT EBITDA: it is underlying net profit attributable to shareholders from leasing + hotels AFTER tax, AFTER all interest (including interest the accounts capitalise into development), AFTER non-controlling interests, BEFORE SBC, over that revenue. FY2025: leasing+hotels underlying attributable 3,278 (3,358 - 80; line 257); less attributable capitalised interest net of tax 706, backed out of the company's own disclosed payout ratios (dividends 2,623 / 3,278 = 80%; 'after deducting amount of interest capitalized' 102% -> 2,623 / 1.02 = 2,572; gross capitalised interest ~HK$984m pre-tax: gross finance costs 1,938 less 920 charged less ~34 interest income) = 2,572; plus 54 SBC = 2,626 / 9,686 = 27.1%. cash_tax_rate is 0 because the stream is already post-tax; D&A is 0 because IAS 40 investment property is not depreciated (hotel/PPE depreciation of HK$150m is already inside underlying profit). Capex line = maintenance/AEI capex (est. 3.85% of revenue, ~HK$373m) plus modest equity-funded growth/AEI (~1.65pp) at steady state, plus the equity-funded share (~70%) of committed development capex in FY2026-28; the remaining ~30% is assumed debt-funded, its interest then sitting in the margin path. last_fcf 2,199 = 2,572 - 373 maintenance: the recurring AFFO analogue before growth capex (HK$0.42/share vs HK$0.52 DPS, which is why ~50-65% of recent final dividends have been taken in scrip). reported_fcf 3,508 is the Metrics.csv FY2025 OCF less capex and is NOT the basis: it is pre-interest-paid, includes inventory/working-capital swings and belongs partly to minorities.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities are immaterial (HK$284m at 30-Jun-2026, interim balance sheet lines 1750/1757) and their interest (HK$7m H1) is inside underlying profit; not added to debt. The Westlake 66 Expansion 20-year head lease (~RMB3.2bn fixed payments from April 2028) and the other 'V.3' asset-light leased projects (Center 66 Expansion, No.1038 West Nanjing Road) carry their own sub-lease rent; treated as value-neutral and not modelled separately, same as the parent 0010.HK build.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, by valuing only the attributable stream: the margin numerator is HLP's own 'underlying net profit attributable to shareholders' (post-NCI) and the capitalised-interest deduction is backed out of attributable payout ratios. No NCI deduction in the bridge (NCI HK$10,420m at 30-Jun-2026). Revenue is consolidated, so NCI sits inside the margin; capex is consolidated too and slightly overstates the attributable charge (NCI ~7% of total equity) -- a small conservative bias left in deliberately. FY0 stream ties to reported underlying net profit attributable (3,202) + property-sales loss add-back (76) - attributable capitalised interest net of tax (706) = 2,572.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in HKD (the flows are post-interest, so discount at CoE, never WACC, and hold net debt at zero): HKD risk-free ~4.0% (HKD peg tracks the USD 10-year), equity beta ~1.0 for a ~32%-geared property company, ERP 5.5%, plus 1.0pp for ~69% of net assets sitting in RMB / mainland China property and regulatory risk = 10.5%. Identical to the parent Hang Lung Group (0010.HK) build so the two valuations are comparable. Same CoE in every scenario so risk is charged once (through the scenario paths and weights).
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md to the REIT / property-trust row (IAS 40 fair-value investment property, internally managed landlord with a smaller trading arm), valued as AFFO-style distributable profit capitalised at cost of equity with net debt held at zero, run through the component engine -- the same method as the parent Hang Lung Group (0010.HK, 64% look-through owner) and Wharf (0004.HK). A consolidated owner-FCF DCF is wrong here: (1) reported FCF (HK$3.5bn FY2025) is pre-interest-paid (HK$1.9bn gross finance cost sits in financing), includes inventory swings, and partly belongs to NCI; (2) statutory net income is dominated by revaluation deficits (FY2025 -1,396 attributable; kpis InvestmentPropertyRevaluation and OperatingProfitAfterRevaluation are NOT used as earnings -- only the company's underlying, revaluation-excluded profit is). The flow valued is post-interest, post-tax, post-minority underlying profit from leasing + hotels with capitalised interest treated as a real expense, less maintenance and equity-funded development capex. HIGH LEVERAGE (net debt HK$47.1bn, ND/E 31.6%, interest cover ~3.1-3.2x, 60% floating): because the stream is after ALL interest, the leverage is charged in the flows, and rising rates or a refinancing at higher spreads would show up as margin compression -- that is the bear axis, not an extra CoE premium. NAV/NTA was considered and rejected as the headline: book NAV is HK$26.6/share (30-Jun-2026) against a price of ~0.25x book; the discount has persisted because the assets earn an underlying ROE of ~2.4% (3,202 / 134,729), so a NAV model would print +300% and be meaningless (the NZL.NZ trap). NAV is a memo only. Property sales are excluded from the recurring stream and valued once in the equity bridge as properties-for-sale inventory at a realisation haircut. No buybacks; scrip dividend is the only issuance. FY0 = FY2025; H1-2026 corroborates the Y1 path: leasing+hotel revenue +5.3% YoY (4,807 -> 5,070), leasing+hotel underlying attributable flat (1,617 -> 1,620) while pre-tax capitalised interest fell 491 -> 389, so the after-capitalised-interest stream rose ~6% and its margin was ~26.8% pre-SBC, slightly below FY0 as Westlake 66 (opened 28-Apr-2026) expenses its interest before its rent matures. First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF.
inputs.nav_memo: Book NAV HK$26.6/share at 30-Jun-2026 (shareholders' equity 138,564 / 5,203m shares); price/book ~0.25x. Not used as the valuation basis (see notes).

base.growth_note: Y1-2 6%: H1-2026 leasing+hotel revenue +5.3% with Westlake 66 open only two months, mainland malls +6% in RMB at 96% occupancy, Plaza 66 Pavilion Extension (H2-26) and Xi Zhe Wuxi hotel (Q3-26) adding; mainland offices (-12% H1) and HK office flat-to-down offset. Fades to 3% as Westlake stabilises and 2.5% long-run (HKD-pegged, RMB-heavy rents).
base.margin_note: FY0 27.1% (post-interest incl. capitalised, post-tax, post-NCI, pre-SBC). Dips to 26.5% in FY2026 as Westlake 66 stops capitalising interest before rent matures (H1-26 run-rate ~26.8%); recovers to 30% by year 7 as Westlake 66, Pavilion Extension and Wuxi hotel lease up on an already-paid-for asset base and the debt balance stops rising once commitments roll off. Average cost of debt 3.8% (FY2025) held.
base.capex_note: FY2026-28 carry the HK$3.9bn IP/PPE commitment tail plus HK$0.9bn JV injections at 30-Jun-2026 (H1-26 already spent HK$1.13bn); ~70% equity-funded. Steady state 5.5% = 3.85% maintenance/AEI + 1.65pp modest equity-funded growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% for concentrated mainland retail/office exposure, a 32%-geared balance sheet with 60% floating-rate debt and ~3x interest cover, and underlying EPS falling ~11%/yr since FY2022; bull cut to 25% because it needs mainland consumption, office absorption, RMB strength and lower rates to all go right; base 50% reflects a stable, highly occupied rental franchise with no refinancing stress. Identical to the parent 0010.HK weights.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
